deep_learning-1.stem: Which libraries are mainly used to build neural networks in Python?
options: TensorFlow and PyTorch
Requests and Flask
Pandas and Seaborn
Selenium and Pytest
deep_learning-1.explanation: TensorFlow/Keras and PyTorch are the main deep-learning frameworks.

deep_learning-2.stem: What is an epoch in neural-network training?
options: One full pass over the training data
One update of a single weight in the long run
One layer of the neural network during the project
One batch of five training examples alone
deep_learning-2.explanation: One full pass of the training data through the model.

deep_learning-3.stem: Which architecture is most commonly used for image classification?
options: Convolutional neural network
Recurrent neural network
Decision tree ensemble
Linear regression model
deep_learning-3.explanation: Convolutional neural networks learn spatial features from images.

deep_learning-4.stem: What is the purpose of dropout?
options: To reduce overfitting by randomly disabling units in training
To reduce overfitting by removing units permanently after training
To speed up training by skipping some batches in each epoch
To normalise the activations of each layer during training
deep_learning-4.explanation: Dropout randomly disables units during training to reduce overfitting.

deep_learning-5.stem: You want to adapt a pretrained language model to your company's support tickets with a small labelled dataset. Which approach is usual?
options: Fine-tune the pretrained model on the labelled tickets from the start
Train a new transformer from random weights on them
Replace the model with a linear regression on the tickets
Delete the pretrained layers and keep just the output layer in a real project
deep_learning-5.explanation: Fine-tune the pretrained model (or use parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA) on your data.

machine_learning-1.stem: Predicting whether an email is spam or not is which kind of task?
options: Classification
Regression
Clustering
Dimensionality reduction

machine_learning-2.stem: Why is a dataset split into training and test sets?
options: To estimate performance on data the model has not seen
To make the training run faster on large files in a real project
To remove duplicated rows from the dataset
To balance the classes before training starts
machine_learning-2.explanation: The test set estimates how the model performs on data it has not seen.

machine_learning-3.stem: A model scores 99% on training data and 70% on test data. What is the most likely problem?
options: Overfitting
Underfitting
Data leakage from the test set
A learning rate that is too low
machine_learning-3.explanation: A large gap between training and test performance indicates overfitting.

machine_learning-4.stem: Only 2% of transactions are fraud. A model that always predicts not fraud has 98% accuracy. Which metric is more informative?
options: Recall and precision for the fraud class
Accuracy over the whole dataset as the work grows
Mean squared error of most of the predictions
R-squared of the fitted line for the business
machine_learning-4.explanation: With imbalanced classes, precision, recall (or F1, PR-AUC) say more than accuracy.

machine_learning-5.stem: You scale features using the mean and standard deviation of the whole dataset before splitting into train and test. What is wrong?
options: Information from the test set leaks into training in a real project
The model will not be able to handle numeric features
The scaling makes the labels lose their meaning
The training set becomes too small for the model to learn from
machine_learning-5.explanation: Statistics from the test data leak into training; fit the scaler on the training set only.

math_for_ml-1.stem: What is the result of multiplying a 2x3 matrix by a 3x4 matrix?
options: A 2x4 matrix
A 3x3 matrix
A 4x2 matrix
The product is not defined
math_for_ml-1.explanation: The inner sizes (3 and 3) match and the result has the outer sizes: 2x4.

math_for_ml-2.stem: The mean of a dataset is 50 and the standard deviation is 10. Roughly what share of values lies between 40 and 60 if the data are normally distributed?
options: About 68%
About 50%
About 95%
About 99.7%
math_for_ml-2.explanation: About 68% of normal data lies within one standard deviation of the mean.

math_for_ml-3.stem: What does the gradient of a loss function point towards?
options: The direction in which the loss increases fastest
The direction in which the loss decreases the fastest
The point where the loss is exactly zero
The average of most the training examples in practice
math_for_ml-3.explanation: The gradient points in the direction of steepest increase of the loss, so training moves the opposite way.

math_for_ml-4.stem: P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.5 and A and B are independent. What is P(A and B)?
math_for_ml-4.explanation: For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 0.15.

math_for_ml-5.stem: A learning rate that is far too large in gradient descent typically causes what?
options: The loss oscillates or diverges in the long run
Training converges more slowly but safely at that stage
The model memorises the training set in most cases
The gradients become exactly zero
math_for_ml-5.explanation: Steps overshoot the minimum, so the loss oscillates or diverges.

mlops_deployment-1.stem: What does it mean to deploy a machine-learning model?
options: Make it available to produce predictions for real use
Retrain it with a larger number of epochs in day-to-day work
Convert its training data to another format as the work grows
Print its accuracy at the end of training during the project
mlops_deployment-1.explanation: Making the trained model available to produce predictions for real users or systems.

mlops_deployment-2.stem: Which tool is commonly used to track experiments and register models?
options: MLflow
Nginx
Terraform
Postman
mlops_deployment-2.explanation: MLflow tracks runs, parameters and metrics and offers a model registry.

mlops_deployment-3.stem: A model's accuracy slowly drops months after launch although the code is unchanged. What is the likely cause?
options: Data or concept drift in the incoming data
A memory leak in the web server
A broken connection to the training server
A compiler optimisation that changes the weights
mlops_deployment-3.explanation: Data drift or concept drift: the real-world data changed.

mlops_deployment-4.stem: Why package a model and its dependencies in a Docker image for serving?
options: The same environment runs in every stage in a real project
The model becomes smaller than its source weights in most teams
The predictions of the model become more accurate
The training time is cut in half
mlops_deployment-4.explanation: The image gives the same environment everywhere, avoiding it works on my machine problems.

mlops_deployment-5.stem: A new model should be tested on live traffic with limited risk. Which release strategy fits?
options: A canary release to a small share of traffic in day-to-day work
Replacing the old model for all of the users at once
Training the new model on the test traffic
Deleting the old model after a code review
mlops_deployment-5.explanation: A canary or shadow deployment sends a small share (or a copy) of traffic to the new model first.

options: Splitting text into words or subword units
Translating text from one language to another
Removing each number from a document
Counting how often a document is read in the long run
nlp_computer_vision-1.explanation: Splitting text into units such as words or subwords.

nlp_computer_vision-2.stem: Which library is widely used for classic image processing such as resizing and edge detection?
options: OpenCV
Scrapy
Celery
Gunicorn
nlp_computer_vision-2.explanation: OpenCV provides image-processing and computer-vision functions.

nlp_computer_vision-3.stem: Word embeddings place words with similar meanings...
options: Close to each other in a vector space
At the same position in a sorted list of words
In separate files by first letter from the start
In the same row of a count table
nlp_computer_vision-3.explanation: In embedding space, words used in similar contexts get nearby vectors.

nlp_computer_vision-4.stem: Which task does an object detection model such as YOLO perform?
options: Locating objects in an image with boxes and labels in practice
Reducing an image to a single colour histogram of its pixels
Converting speech in a video into text
Translating the captions of an image
nlp_computer_vision-4.explanation: It locates objects with bounding boxes and labels them.

nlp_computer_vision-5.stem: A sentiment classifier trained on product reviews is used on tweets and does much worse. What is this?
options: Domain shift between training and deployment data
Overfitting to the number of training epochs that was used
A bug in the tokeniser vocabulary file as the work grows
Class imbalance in the test labels in practice for the business
nlp_computer_vision-5.explanation: Domain shift: the data distribution changed between training and use.
